source_text: Clarificatio enim domini nostri apud homines resurrectio est a mortuis et in caelum ascensio. scriptum est autem in ipso euangelio xaxa \'IcorivvTjv: spiritus autem nondum erat datus, quia Iesus nondum erat clarificatus. si ergo propterea nondum erat datus, quia Iesus nondum erat clarificatus, clarificato Iesu necessario statim datus est. et propter ipsam geminam clarificationem, secundum hominem et secundum deum, bis datus est etiam spiritus sanctus: semel, postquam resurrexit a mortuis, cum insufflauit in faciem discipulorum dicens: accipite spiritum sanctum; et iterum, postquam ascendit in caelum decem diebus transactis: qui numerus perfectionem significat, cum septenario numero. quo condita uniuersa consistunt, additur trinitas conditoris. de quibus rebus inter spiritales uiros pie cauteque multa tractantur. sed ego a proposito non recedam; suscepi enim prius uobiscum sic agere, ut non uos ego doceam, quod superbum fortasse arbitramini. sed tamquam ipse a uobis discere studeam, quod nouem annis non potui. quapropter habeo, quibus litteris credam de aduentu spiritus sancti: quibus me credere si prohibetis, ne temere credam quod nescio — sic enim soletis monere —, multo minus uestris litteris credam. quare aut omnes libros auferte de medio et disputando pandite ueritatem, de qua dubitare non possim, aut tales proferte libros, quibus non mihi cum adrogantia inponatur, quod credam, sed exhibeatur sine fraude. quod discam. fortasse. inquis, et haec epistula talis est. nolo ergo in eius limine ulterius inmorari: interiora uideamus.
thought_title: The Spirit Given After Christ's Glorification
orientation: Augustine is still arguing from the Acts of the Apostles that the Holy Spirit was demonstrably sent to the true apostles, and now turns to the Gospel of John to show the Spirit was given after Jesus was glorified.
pass_a_gloss: For the glorification of our Lord among men is the resurrection from the dead and the ascension into heaven. But it is written in the Gospel itself according to John: 'the Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.' If therefore it was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified, when Jesus was glorified it was necessarily given at once. And on account of that very double glorification, according to man and according to God, the Holy Spirit was also given twice: once, after he rose from the dead, when he breathed into the face of the disciples saying: 'receive the Holy Spirit'; and again, after he ascended into heaven, ten days having passed: which number signifies perfection, when to the sevenfold number, by which all created things consist, is added the Trinity of the Creator. About these matters many things are treated piously and cautiously among spiritual men. But I will not depart from my purpose; for I have undertaken first to deal with you in such a way that I do not teach you, which you perhaps consider arrogant, but as if I myself were eager to learn from you what I could not in nine years. Therefore I have writings which I may believe about the coming of the Holy Spirit: if you forbid me to believe these, lest I rashly believe what I do not know — for so you are accustomed to warn — I will believe your writings much less. Therefore either take away all books from the midst and by disputing lay open the truth, about which I cannot doubt, or bring forth such books by which what I am to believe is not imposed on me with arrogance, but what I am to learn is shown without deceit. Perhaps, you say, this letter is also such. I do not wish therefore to linger any longer on its threshold: let us see the inner parts.

choices.why: The noun corresponds to the verb 'clarifico' used in the quoted Gospel verse; 'glorification' keeps the verbal link clear.

choices.english: according to man and according to God
choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the theological distinction Augustine draws between Christ's two natures.
rejected: in his humanity and in his divinity

choices.english: when he breathed into the face of the disciples
choices.why: Literal rendering of the physical action described in John 20:22.
rejected: when he blew on the disciples' faces
when he breathed on the disciples

choices.why: Ablative absolute rendered literally to preserve the temporal construction.

choices.english: to linger any longer on its threshold
choices.why: The metaphor of a doorway or entrance is important for Augustine's argument about Mani's letter; 'threshold' keeps the image.

pass_b_english: The glorification of our Lord among human beings is his resurrection from the dead and his ascension into heaven. In the gospel itself it is written, according to John: “The Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified” (John 7:39). If the Spirit had not yet been given for this reason, because Jesus had not yet been glorified, then once Jesus was glorified the Spirit was necessarily given at once. And because of that twofold glorification, according to man and according to God, the Holy Spirit was also given twice: once after he rose from the dead, when he breathed into the face of the disciples and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22); and again after he ascended into heaven, ten days having passed. That number signifies perfection, since the Trinity of the Creator is added to the sevenfold number by which all created things hold together. Spiritual men discuss many things about these matters with reverence and care. But I will not depart from my purpose. I undertook to deal with you in such a way that I would not teach you—which you perhaps consider arrogant—but that I would seem to be eager to learn from you what I could not learn in nine years. So I have writings I can believe about the coming of the Holy Spirit. If you forbid me to believe them, so that I do not rashly believe what I do not know—for that is how you usually warn—then I will believe your writings far less. So either take all books out of the way and by arguing lay open the truth, about which I cannot doubt, or produce books of such a kind that what I am to believe is not imposed on me with arrogance, but what I am to learn is shown to me without deceit. Perhaps, you say, this letter is such a book. I do not want to linger any longer on its threshold. Let us look at what is inside.

last_rejected.quote: but that I would seem to be eager to learn from you what I could not learn in nine years
last_rejected.source_quote: tamquam ipse a uobis discere studeam
last_rejected.why: Source: 'as though I myself were eager to learn from you'; English 'I would seem' misplaces the 'as if' and 'tamquam' scope, sense roughly fine but garbled; also 'sed' contrast lost.
last_rejected.fix: but as though I myself were eager to learn from you what I could not learn in nine years
last_rejected.ruling: “tamquam…studeam” is “as though I were eager,” and “seem” is loose, but “but” keeps sed and the learner-stance.
